title: Build a second voice in thirds
context: Synthetic C-major phrase · proposed upper diatonic third · time in beats
caption: Teaching proposal in C major: over C4–D4–E4–F4, add E4–F4–G4–A4. The gaps are 4, 3, 3, 4 semitones: diatonic thirds change size. Toggle the second voice visually; audition the separate WAV/MIDI and check the actual chords and singer's range.

notes.comment: C4 + E4: a major third, four semitones. Check that E fits the actual chord before using this proposal.
D4 + F4: a minor third, three semitones. A fixed +4 shift would give F#, outside C major.
E4 + G4: another minor third. Scale membership alone does not prove the pair suits the accompaniment.
F4 + A4: a major third. Audition the full phrase and check chord movement, phrasing and vocal range.

actions.label: Ask agent: explain this second voice
actions.prompt: Explain the synthetic C-major second-voice proposal: melody C4–D4–E4–F4 and upper voice E4–F4–G4–A4. Describe why the third alternates between four and three semitones and why actual chord context/range still need checking. Treat this as a teaching proposal, not verified transcription. Answer in the conversation language.
